name: Question 3
problem: Find the inverse of the function $f(x)=\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{x}}-4.$
worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{x}}-4
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}}-4.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}}-4 \\ x+4 & =\frac{2}{3\sqrt[3]{y}} \\ \frac{1}{x+4} & =\frac{3\sqrt[3]{y}}{2} \\ \sqrt[3]{y} & =\frac{2}{3(x+4)} \\ (\sqrt[3]{y})^{3} & ={(\frac{2}{3(x+4)})}^{3} \\ y & =\frac{8}{27(x+4)^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{8}{27(x+4)^{3}}.
$$

**Note**: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are

$$
x\ne 0,\,f(x)\ne -4.
$$

Therefore, the domain and range of ${f}^{-1}(x)$ are

$$
x\ne -4,\,{f}^{-1}(x)\ne 0.
$$
